newsitem.title: USA: Proposed Pa. budget sees 2.7 pct spending rise.
newsitem.headline: Proposed Pa. budget sees 2.7 pct spending rise.

text.p: Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Ridge Tuesday proposed a fiscal 1997-1998 budget that calls for a 2.7 percent increase in spending levels, $67 million in tax cuts, and increased aid to school districts.
Total general-fund spending in the budget is proposed at $16.9 billion, up from $16.4 billion in 1996-1997, according to figures released by Ridge's office.

Included in the tax cut proposals is a $25 million cut in personal income taxes for working poor families, by increasing to $4,000 from $3,000 a dependent exemption under a low-income tax-forgiveness program.
The cut would eliminate the income tax for a family of four earning about $18,000 a year, saving about $500 from current levels.
The cut will affect about 80,000 families.

Ridge also proposed a $9.7 million cut in a state capital stock and franchise tax on businesses, a $21.8 million exemption -- applicable to manufacturing, processing and agricultural industries -- in sales taxes on computer services, and a $10 million research and development tax credit.
The budget proposes a 3 percent, $100 million increase in the basic schools subsidy, $10 million of which would be awarded on the basis of performance gains.
Other programs increase school spending by $48 million, and districts will save $51 million in required contributions to a state retirement program, according to the proposal.
